subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When blood glucose rises after a meal, insulin lowers it by:
options: Increasing the uptake of glucose by cells and promoting glycogenesis
Converting amino acids and glycerol into glucose
Stimulating glycogenolysis in the liver
Inhibiting respiration in muscle cells
questions.explain: Insulin raises glucose uptake (via more GLUT4 channels) and promotes glycogenesis, converting glucose to glycogen for storage.

questions.q: What is the approximate respiratory quotient (RQ) for the complete aerobic respiration of a carbohydrate such as glucose?
questions.explain: For glucose the volumes of CO2 produced and O2 consumed are equal, giving an RQ of 1.0.

questions.q: Why does reduced FAD ultimately lead to the synthesis of fewer ATP molecules than reduced NAD?
options: FAD is not used by the electron transport chain
FAD carries no electrons, only protons
FAD donates its electrons at a later point on the chain, pumping fewer protons
FAD is produced only in the cytoplasm
questions.explain: FAD feeds electrons in further along the chain than NAD, so fewer protons are pumped and less ATP is made.

questions.q: What is the immediate source of the electrons that replace those lost from photosystem II during non-cyclic photophosphorylation?
options: The photolysis of water
Carbon dioxide fixation
Reduced NADP
ATP hydrolysis
questions.explain: Photolysis splits water, supplying electrons to photosystem II as well as protons and oxygen.

questions.q: Where in the mitochondrion are the electron carriers of the electron transport chain located?
options: The inner membrane (cristae)
The outer membrane
The matrix
The intermembrane space
questions.explain: The chain of carriers is embedded in the folded inner mitochondrial membrane, the cristae.

questions.q: Glucagon raises blood glucose principally by stimulating:
options: The conversion of glucose to fat
Glycogenesis and glucose uptake
Glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis in the liver
Insulin secretion from beta cells
questions.explain: Glucagon promotes breakdown of glycogen (glycogenolysis) and synthesis of glucose from non-carbohydrate sources (gluconeogenesis) in the liver.

questions.q: The counter-current multiplier in the loop of Henle works because:
options: Both limbs are equally permeable to water and ions
The ascending limb actively pumps out sodium ions, creating a high solute concentration (low water potential) in the medulla
The ascending limb is permeable to water but not ions
The descending limb actively pumps in water
questions.explain: Active removal of Na+ from the impermeable-to-water ascending limb builds a medullary solute gradient that draws water out of the descending limb and collecting duct.

questions.q: How does anaerobic fermentation in yeast differ from that in mammalian muscle?
options: Yeast produces lactate; muscle produces ethanol
Yeast uses oxygen whereas muscle does not
Yeast produces ethanol and CO2; muscle produces lactate
Both produce ethanol but only muscle releases CO2
questions.explain: Yeast decarboxylates pyruvate and reduces it to ethanol, releasing CO2, whereas mammalian muscle forms lactate.

questions.q: Negative feedback in homeostasis acts to:
options: Amplify a deviation from the set point
Maintain a constant rate of change
Switch off all hormone secretion permanently
Reverse a change and return a factor toward its set point
questions.explain: Negative feedback detects a deviation and triggers responses that oppose it, restoring the internal environment toward the set point.

questions.q: Which statement correctly summarises where the two main stages of photosynthesis occur?
options: Both stages occur in the stroma
Light-dependent in the thylakoids; light-independent in the stroma
Light-dependent in the stroma; light-independent in the thylakoids
Both stages occur on the thylakoid membranes
questions.explain: The light reactions occur on the thylakoid membranes and the Calvin cycle occurs in the stroma.

questions.q: In the Calvin cycle, which enzyme catalyses the fixation of carbon dioxide onto RuBP?
options: Decarboxylase
Dehydrogenase
ATP synthase
RuBisCO
questions.explain: RuBisCO catalyses the combination of CO2 with ribulose bisphosphate to form two molecules of GP.

questions.q: Which statement about the role of reduced NAD and reduced FAD in respiration is correct?
options: They deliver electrons and protons to the electron transport chain
They are produced only during oxidative phosphorylation
They are the final electron acceptors of the chain
They directly phosphorylate ADP to ATP
questions.explain: Reduced coenzymes carry electrons and protons to the carriers on the inner membrane, feeding the chain.
